title: hierarchical-lane-scheduler: opportunistic comm/compute interleaving with soft-priority NCCL lanes
author: Asha Mehta
release_notes: Introduces a hierarchical NCCL lane scheduler and opportunistic comm/compute interleaving. Default-off behind runtime flag; improves TP throughput and p99 latency in heterogeneous-batch workloads. See ENG-1987 for rollout plan.
description: Motivation: tensor-parallel workloads experience stalls when collectives and kernel launches contend for GPU resources and when KV cache prefetches interfere with in-flight NCCL streams. This PR implements a hierarchical lane scheduler that classifies NCCL lanes into soft-priority groups and uses opportunistic kernel launch windows to interleave communication and compute while preserving correctness. The goal is to reduce comm-induced stalls, improve kernel packing for small microbatches, and prioritize KV-cache prefetches that unblock the critical path. Summary of changes: 1) scheduler: hierarchical_lane_scheduler module that creates lane classes (control/high/low) and maintains per-peer credit accounting and vacancy windows; 2) nccl: soft-priority lane construction with graceful demotion/promotion heuristics and lane affinity hints on collective enqueue; 3) kvcache: prioritized prefetch queue integration so hot-shard prefetches use high-priority lanes and do not starve reduce/allgather operations; 4) batching: continuous-batcher boundary awareness so the scheduler respects microbatch commit windows and coalesces kernel launches when safe; 5) telemetry: new metrics (tp.lane.waits, tp.lane.promotions, tp.kv.prefetch_blocked) and corresponding console panels for debugging. Design notes: the lane scheduler uses a lightweight token/credit model and a small state machine per-lane to avoid global locks. Promotion is heuristic-driven (time-in-limbo, backlog, peer-progress) and conservative to avoid starvation. All new behavior is gated behind runtime config flags --runtime.experimental.hierarchical_lanes and --runtime.experimental.kv_lane_priority and is off by default in production clusters. Benchmarks: on a mix of 8xA100 TP tests (seq_len=2048, batch=2 microbatching=8) we observed +18% sustained throughput for throughput-bound prompts, 12% reduction in p99 tail latency on short-response workloads, and ~6% reduction in token GPU time cost on mixed workloads. Safety and fallbacks: if NCCL returns transient errors or lane contention exceeds thresholds, the scheduler demotes lanes to round-robin mode and records diagnostic traces for post-mortem. Rollout: staged canary on Dedicated regions for 2 weeks behind feature flag, monitor tp.lane.* metrics and rollback on regression. Implementation detail highlights: - We do not change NCCL kernels; changes are orchestration and enqueue-time hints. - KV cache prefetch now provides an affinity hint so the runtime routes it through high-priority async lanes. - Continuous batcher cooperates with the scheduler by emitting a small token when a microbatch boundary is safe to coalesce. The description below includes commits, diffs, review thread, and CI history for context.

review_comments: Diego Ramos (2026-02-11): The promotion heuristics look promising but I'm worried about oscillation under bursty traffic. Can we add a decay window to avoid thundering promotions?
Asha Mehta (2026-02-11): Added a decay_time_ms parameter and unit tests. Promotion now requires consecutive conditions over a small window. See commit 9b3c1a4.
Xiao Chen (2026-02-12): Can you clarify how prefetch affinity interacts with existing cache eviction policy? We don't want high-priority prefetches to thrash the hot-set.

Asha Mehta (2026-02-12): Prefetch affinity only affects transport lane, not placement policy. Eviction policy unchanged; added a comment and test to ensure prefetch entries are subject to the same LRU heuristics.
Priya Nair (2026-02-13): Telemetry looks useful. Please add an alert for tp.lane.promotions > 50/min in the canary run so we can detect oscillation early.
Asha Mehta (2026-02-13): Added alert rule and onboarding note in docs. Also added a flag to throttle promotions if the metric exceeds threshold.
Diego Ramos (2026-02-15): Verified integration on local 4xV100 sim; requesting one more perf run on 8xA100 canary before merge.
Asha Mehta (2026-02-16): Perf run uploaded to docs/perf/bench_results. Observed +18% throughput under targeted workload. Pushing fix for a rare NCCL ordering test failure (commit 7ab9d6e).
Xiao Chen (2026-02-17): Code looks clean and tests cover edge cases I was worried about. Approving.

merge_details: Merged by Priya Nair on 2026-02-18 via squash-merge. Merge commit message: 'hierarchical lane scheduler + nccl soft-priority lanes: opportunistic comm/compute interleaving (ENG-1987)'. Feature gated behind runtime flags for staged rollout.
notes_for_operators: Feature is off by default. To enable in Dedicated canary: set --runtime.experimental.hierarchical_lanes=true and --runtime.experimental.kv_lane_priority=true, monitor tp.lane.* metrics and tp.kv.prefetch_blocked alerts. If regressions observed, set flag to false and escalate to infrastructure SREs with collected logs (tp_lane.trace).
rollback_plan: If canary shows increased p99 or promotion storms, flip both feature flags off. A follow-up hotfix (if needed) will revert the scheduling registration path to round-robin and disable affinity hints in NCCL enqueue.
testing_notes: Includes unit tests for scheduler state machine and integration microbench. Added a deterministic NCCL sim harness for CI. Perf numbers captured in docs/perf/bench_results/2026-02-hierarchical-lanes.md.
